question: A dealer allowed a 23% discount on an article and was still able to manage a 44% profit. Find the ratio of the cost price to the listed price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume CP = 100

Profit = 44% ⇒ SP = 144

Discount = 23% ⇒ SP = 77% of MP

MP = 144 ÷ 0.77 = 14400 ÷ 77

Ratio CP : MP = 100 : (14400/77) = 77 : 144

**∴ Answer = 77 : 144**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount = 23%, Profit = 44%

**Formula used:**

SP = MP × (1 − Discount/100), SP = CP × (1 + Profit/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let CP = 100

⇒ SP = 100 × 1.44 = 144

⇒ SP = MP × 77/100

⇒ 144 = MP × 77/100

⇒ MP = (144 × 100) ÷ 77 = 14400/77

⇒ Ratio CP : MP = 100 : (14400/77)

⇒ Multiply by 77 ⇒ 7700 : 14400

⇒ Simplify ⇒ 77 : 144

**∴ The correct answer is 77 : 144.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation Between CP, SP and MP

SP = CP × (1 + profit%) and SP = MP × (1 − discount%).

Assumption Method

Taking CP = 100 simplifies percentage calculations.

Ratio Simplification

Convert ratios into integers by multiplying with common denominator.
